name: Punch Volley
summary: A punch volley takes the ball out of the air at the kitchen line with a short forward push, no backswing. It is the plainest attacking shot in pickleball and the one recreational players most often turn into a full swing. Direction and a low contact point beat pace every time.
whenToUse: A ball is coming at you at or above net height and you are set at the kitchen line.
The opponents have popped a dink up and you want it back at their feet immediately.
You are in a hands battle and there is no time for anything longer.
You want to keep the ball in play with pace rather than gamble on a winner.
howTo: Start with the paddle up in front of your chest, tip above the wrist.
Take the ball in front of your body, never beside your hip.
Push forward from the shoulder about a foot — that is the entire stroke.
Keep the face slightly closed so the ball travels down rather than out.
Aim at the closest opponent's feet or hip, not at the open court.
Bring the paddle straight back to the middle for the next one.
commonMistakes: Taking a backswing, which is both too slow and sends the ball long.
Letting the ball get beside or behind you, at which point only a defensive flick is left.
Punching a ball that was below net height, which puts it into the tape.
Aiming at the sideline for a winner when their feet were the higher-percentage target.
Dropping the paddle after contact instead of resetting it.

drills.name: No backswing
drills.description: Your partner feeds a steady stream of chest-high balls from their kitchen. You punch every one back at their hip. Have them watch your paddle and stop the drill any time it goes behind your body.

drills.name: Feet, not lines
drills.description: Same feed, but score only punches that land inside the kitchen or on the feeder's shoes. Balls that land deep in the court score nothing even if they would have been winners.

mistake.label: Swung at with a backswing: the extra pace carries it past their feet and deep enough to be comfortable.
